text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chief Justice Majid Cockar, Appeal Judge Richard Kwach and the Law Society of Kenya agree on measures to streamline the judiciary and establish a new court to ease congestion at the High Court.
- There are reports of boycotts, confusion and fighting on the third day of Kenya's voter registration drive.
- Local businessman George Alan Doig, proprietor of Bunson Travel is found dead in his Muthaiga home in Nairobi.
- National Electoral Commission Chairman Zacchaeus Chesoni claims that a group of people have invaded registration centres with the aim of rigging the forthcoming general elections.
- Fourteen people narrowly escape death when a vehicle they had hired to transport them to a voter's registration centre in Mombasa, is torched by a gang, wielding machetes.
- British immigration officials deport a Kenyan found in possession of a forged British passport.
- President Daniel arap Moi calls for ruling party grassroot elections in Nairobi branch for Thursday and Friday next week.
- City hawkers defy a Nairobi City Council directive to move out of the city's central business district.
- Athi River Mining Limited is given a three-month ultimatum to control dust emitted by their plant or close down. ($1=54 Kenya Shillings)
